results.name: A · exactly ONE row offers the die, and it is the cloak  <-- THIS IS THE SLICE
results.detail: «+1d10 retaliation» on the Flaming Cloak row

results.name: A · and before anything is recorded it says "none yet", not a zero
results.detail: the row reads "none yet" — a 0 reads as a measurement ("the cloak has done nothing"); the truth is that nothing has been written down yet, and at a table those are different facts

results.name: B · the tap ROLLED — a whole number between 1 and 10, from the app’s own d10
results.detail: the strip opened carrying 1 — canon says 1d10, so 1..10 is the whole range

results.name: B · and it is an EDITABLE TEXT FIELD, not a label  <-- MARCUS’S ANSWER
results.detail: type=text inputmode=numeric editable=true — half the time the die that decides this is a real d10 on a real table and the app cannot see it. type="number" was rejected on purpose: it reports "" mid-edit, which would flicker Add off between the 1 and the 2 of a 12.

results.name: C · the tally reads the number he TYPED, not the number the app rolled
results.detail: the app rolled 1; he typed 7; the row says "TOTAL 7 Fire over 1 hit"

results.name: C · the strip closed behind it — the number is recorded, not still pending
results.detail: back to the standing button, with the total beside it

results.name: C · and it counts HITS as well as damage
results.detail: «TOTAL 7 Fire over 1 hit» — the count is what tells him the app MISSED one, which is the failure mode of any tally a human has to remember to tap

results.name: D · Cancel records nothing and leaves the total where it was
results.detail: after rolling and cancelling, the row still reads "TOTAL 7 Fire over 1 hit"

results.name: D · leaving the app’s own roll alone records THAT number, to the point
results.detail: rolled 8, added untouched, and 7 + 8 = 15: the row reads "TOTAL 15 Fire over 2 hits"

results.name: D · and it survives a reload — the DM’s number outlives the tab
results.detail: after a full page reload the row still reads "TOTAL 15 Fire over 2 hits"

results.name: E · with no temp HP at all, the standing button is unchanged  <-- MARCUS’S ANSWER
results.detail: «+1d10 retaliation» — the prompt is the convenience, this is the guarantee, and a guarantee with a condition on it is not one

results.name: E · and logging damage with the cloak down offers nothing
results.detail: no prompt, correctly: there is no live pool for the cloak to have absorbed anything with

results.name: F · logging damage while the cloak is up asks, in the feature’s own name
results.detail: «Hearthfire Manifest — roll 1d10 retaliation?» under the HP tracker (inBand=false), answerable Yes or No

results.name: F · Yes rolls, the number is correctable here too, and Add takes it away
results.detail: the prompt rolled 2, took a typed 9 over it, and dismissed itself on Add

results.name: F · and it feeds the SAME tally the band shows — one number, two routes
results.detail: the reactions band now reads "TOTAL 9 Fire over 1 hit" for a hit logged on the HP tracker — both controls dispatch the same event to the same reducer

results.name: G · the button is there out of combat too — it is genuinely unconditional
results.detail: «+1d10 retaliation»

results.name: G · the refusal is PAINTED, in the reducer’s own words
results.detail: «Start the encounter before recording retaliation damage.»

results.name: G · and the number he typed is still in the field, waiting
results.detail: the field still reads "7" — the fix is "start the encounter, press Add again", not "roll it a second time and hope it comes up 7"

results.name: G · and nothing was recorded — the refusal refused
results.detail: with the strip closed the row reads "none yet": a refused Add leaves no total behind, which is the point of refusing it — "per encounter" is meaningless with no encounter, and a tally opened here is one the next startCombat wipes

results.name: H · nothing in the band trails off
results.detail: the phase’s standing claim, re-measured on the surface this slice changed

results.name: H · clean console
results.detail: no errors
